name: Codex Chat via App-Server ("protocol-first"): headless codex app-server sessions rendered as a native chat surface, PTY demoted to escape hatch
coreIdea: Stop scraping ANSI. Spawn `codex app-server` (stdio JSON-RPC, the officially documented integration surface that powers the VS Code extension) from the Rust backend — one supervised process per account/workspace, using the exact spawn pattern that already exists in settings.rs::read_server_rate_limits (CODEX_HOME env, stdin kept open, newline-delimited JSON). The backend translates app-server notifications (item/started, item/agentMessage/delta, item/commandExecution/outputDelta, item/completed, turn/*, approval requests) into a single new event `codex-event` mirrored over both transports (Tauri emit on desktop, one WebSocket in server.rs for web), and exposes a small command family (chat_open_thread, chat_send, chat_interrupt, chat_approve...). The frontend gains a new primary AppView "chat" built with the app's own proven patterns: the Agent Room's targeted-innerHTML feed + composer (#roomFeed/#roomComposer at main.ts renderRoomPanel/refreshRoom), not a framework migration. Item lifecycle drives card rendering exactly like OpenCode: card created on item/started, streamed into via deltas, finalized on item/completed; approvals are inline blocking cards replying on the JSON-RPC request id. The raw PTY terminal stays as-is as a secondary view and a per-thread escape hatch (`codex resume <rolloutId>` in a real terminal, reusing buildResumeCommand). History backfills from thread/read plus the existing rollout-JSONL machinery in discussions.rs (collapse_forks/find_rollout_by_id).
architecture: DESKTOP FLOW — user input to rendered message: (1) User types in #chatComposer (new renderChatPanel() branch in src/main.ts, added to the AppView union at L365 and setActiveView at L1418, listeners wired in bindUi() L3915). (2) Submit calls invoke("chat_send", {threadKey, text}) through src/platform.ts's existing invoke() facade. (3) New module src-tauri/src/codex_agent.rs (registered in lib.rs invoke_handler next to the 30 existing commands) holds AppServerManager (Tauri managed state, like TerminalManager in terminal.rs): a HashMap<threadKey, AppServerSession> where each session owns a child `codex app-server` process spawned with CODEX_HOME=<account.codex_home> (env/spawn code lifted from settings.rs::read_server_rate_limits L1275-1434, which already solved the codex>=0.144 keep-stdin-open quirk), a pending-request id map, and a stdout reader thread. chat_send issues turn/start (or turn/steer if a turn is active) over stdin. (4) The reader thread parses each JSONL notification, wraps it in a compact envelope {threadKey, method, params: serde_json::Value} and calls app.emit("codex-event", envelope) — the exact pattern of terminal.rs's pty-data emit at L235. Server->client JSON-RPC requests (item/commandExecution/requestApproval, item/fileChange/requestApproval, tool/requestUserInput) are parked in the pending map and forwarded as codex-event with their request id; the UI answers via invoke("chat_approve", {threadKey, requestId, decision}). (5) In src/main.ts setupEvents() (L4745), a new listen("codex-event") sits beside listen("pty-data") and dispatches to applyCodexEvent(), which does targeted DOM patching of #chatFeed keyed by item id (create card on item/started, append text on item/agentMessage/delta rendered through a bundled markdown+sanitizer, stream command output into a <pre> on item/commandExecution/outputDelta, finalize on item/completed; turn/diff/updated feeds a collapsible "Changements" panel; thread/tokenUsage/updated feeds the statusbar). #chatFeed lives inside section.terminal-shell and survives full render() rebuilds via the same detach/reattach trick mountActiveTerminal() (L4521) uses for xterm elements. WEB FLOW: server.rs (already the 1:1 HTTP mirror) adds POST /api/chat/threads|/api/chat/:key/send|approve|interrupt plus a multiplexed WS /ws/chat?token= that forwards the same envelopes, with the parked-broadcast-receiver replay pattern already used by /ws/terminals/:id; src/platform.ts adds the matching cases in the remoteInvoke() switch (L210) and an openChatSocket() that re-emits frames as "codex-event" through the existing emit()/listeners map — so main.ts is transport-agnostic, identical to how pty-data works today. HISTORY: on thread open, backfill via thread/read (app-server) or, for cold sessions, a new get_discussion_transcript command in discussions.rs reusing collapse_forks/parse_rollout_filename to render past user_message/agent_message events. Codex TS types are generated at build time with `codex app-server generate-ts --out src/generated` pinned to the installed CLI version.
phases: PHASE 1 — Rust app-server supervisor (desktop only). Files: new src-tauri/src/codex_agent.rs; src-tauri/src/lib.rs (register commands + managed state); src-tauri/src/settings.rs (factor the codex-binary+CODEX_HOME spawn helper out of read_server_rate_limits for reuse; make ensure_codex_bypass_config conditional so chat mode can run with approvals ON while PTY mode keeps bypass). Commands: chat_open_thread({accountId, projectDir, resumeRolloutId?}) -> threadKey (does spawn + initialize/initialized handshake + thread/start|thread/resume), chat_send, chat_interrupt, chat_approve, chat_close_thread, chat_list_models. Notifications forwarded verbatim-but-enveloped as app.emit("codex-event", {threadKey, method, params}); unknown methods passed through, never crash. Process lifecycle: kill child on chat_close_thread and on app exit (Drop), restart-on-crash with a codex-event system notice. ACCEPTANCE: with no UI changes, a devtools invoke("chat_open_thread")+invoke("chat_send") streams item/agentMessage/delta events into a console listener; chat_interrupt stops a running turn; process count returns to zero after close; JSON-RPC -32001 surfaces as a typed error event.

PHASE 2 — Chat view MVP in the frontend. Files: src/main.ts (add "chat" to AppView union L365, setActiveView L1418, render() branch L2457, bindUi() L3915, setupEvents() L4745 listen("codex-event"), new ChatThread state array + applyCodexEvent() targeted patcher modeled on refreshRoom()'s atBottom-preserving innerHTML swap L1310); src/style.css (new .chat-* rules AFTER the Event Horizon layer at L3003, consuming --panel/--line/--text/--accent/--radius tokens). Plain-text bubbles only: user message, streaming assistant message, running/idle turn indicator, Stop button (chat_interrupt), composer with Enter-to-send + Shift+Enter newline. #chatFeed DOM kept outside the full-rebuild path via detach/reattach exactly like mountActiveTerminal(). ACCEPTANCE: send a prompt, watch tokens stream into the bubble with no flicker across a render() (e.g. toggle another view and back); composer focus and feed scroll survive re-renders; French UI strings; works with 2 simultaneous threads on 2 accounts.

PHASE 3 — Rich cards, approvals, markdown. Files: src/main.ts (card renderers per item type: agentMessage [markdown], reasoning [collapsible 'reflexion'], commandExecution [command + streamed output <pre> + exit code], fileChange [per-file diff], plan [checklist from turn/plan/updated], mcpToolCall, webSearch; approval cards for item/commandExecution/requestApproval + item/fileChange/requestApproval with Accepter/Accepter pour la session/Refuser buttons -> chat_approve, and tool/requestUserInput question cards); package.json + vite bundling of marked + DOMPurify (CSP forbids CDN — must be bundled; everything else stays escapeHtml'd); src/style.css. Statusbar chips from thread/tokenUsage/updated and account/rateLimits/updated. Settings: per-account chat approval policy (bypass=chat-off by default) round-tripped through AppSettings in settings.rs. ACCEPTANCE: a prompt that edits a file produces a fileChange diff card and a blocking approval card whose Accept lets the turn proceed; command output streams live; markdown tables/code render sanitized (script injection test passes); reasoning is collapsed by default with a toggle.

PHASE 4 — History, sidebar unification, persistence. Files: src-tauri/src/discussions.rs (new get_discussion_transcript(accountId, sessionId) reusing find_rollout_by_id/collapse_forks and the contains-then-parse line pattern, returning typed user/agent/tool events from the HEAD rollout); src/main.ts (sidebar .terminal-side-list shows chat threads and PTY terminals as distinct session kinds; Discussions view gains 'Ouvrir en chat' via thread/resume next to the existing resume-in-terminal; persist open chat threads in localStorage alongside OPEN_TERMINALS_STORAGE_KEY L573 and restore on boot like restoreTerminals() L2100). ACCEPTANCE: restart the app, previously open chat threads reappear with full backfilled transcript and can continue; an old discussion opens as a readable chat transcript in <1s for a 500-message session.

PHASE 5 — Web/SaaS parity. Files: src-tauri/src/server.rs (mount codex_agent behind /api/chat/* + WS /ws/chat with check_admin_header auth — NOT forgotten, since auth is per-handler — and the parked-receiver replay pattern from handle_terminal_socket for reconnect backfill); src/platform.ts (remoteInvoke() switch cases for the 6 chat commands at L210; openChatSocket() emitting "codex-event" via the internal emit() bus at ~L577; reconnect-with-backfill since chat, unlike xterm, cannot tolerate silent stream death). ACCEPTANCE: full phase-2/3 flows work in a browser against cst-server including approvals; killing the WS mid-turn reconnects and replays missed events; a node without the chat routes degrades gracefully (feature-detect, hide chat).

PHASE 6 — Flip the default surface, demote the terminal. Files: src/main.ts (New-session modal defaults to 'Chat' with 'Terminal brut' as explicit choice; topbar per-thread 'Ouvrir dans le terminal' escape hatch that closes the app-server thread then runs buildResumeCommand(rolloutId) L661 in a fresh PTY — never both at once, guarded to avoid rollout-file contention; Skill buttons L~3900 retargeted to the chat composer when a chat thread is active); README.md + docs. ACCEPTANCE: fresh install lands in chat; a chat thread can be handed off to a raw terminal and back (via re-resume) without transcript corruption; all 8 legacy views and plain-shell PTY sessions still work untouched.
keepsRawTerminal: Fully. The PTY pipeline (terminal.rs, pty-data/pty-exit, xterm.js sessions, /ws/terminals/:id) is not modified — chat threads and PTY terminals become two coexisting session kinds in the same sidebar. The terminal remains (a) the surface for plain shells and non-Codex CLI agents (AgentProfile kind cli), (b) an explicit 'Terminal brut' option in the new-session modal, and (c) a per-thread escape hatch: 'Ouvrir dans le terminal' closes the app-server thread and launches `codex resume <rolloutId>` in a real PTY via the existing buildResumeCommand/startTerminalSession path (with a mutual-exclusion guard so app-server and the TUI never write the same session concurrently). Nothing about the migration deletes terminal code; the flip in Phase 6 only changes the default.
risks: app-server is labeled Experimental and its schema is version-pinned: a codex CLI upgrade can rename notifications or change item shapes. Mitigations: envelope-and-ignore-unknown-methods in Rust, generate-ts pinned at build time, runtime feature detection from the initialize response — but breakage risk on user-managed codex installs is real (users update codex independently of this app).

Approvals conflict with the app's baked-in bypass: ensure_codex_bypass_config writes approval_policy=never + sandbox_mode=danger-full-access into every account's config.toml, and bypass defaults to true. Chat approval cards are meaningless unless bypass becomes mode-conditional (Phase 1/3), and changing config.toml semantics touches PTY behavior too — needs careful per-mode gating and settings migration.

Dual-transport parity tax: every chat feature needs Tauri command + server.rs route/WS + platform.ts mapping. Skipping any leg silently breaks web mode (existing precedent: list_prompt_history is already stubbed empty remotely). Phase 5 must be treated as mandatory, not polish; also new server routes are unauthenticated by default (per-handler auth) — an easy security regression.

main.ts render() rebuilds all of #app via innerHTML; a streaming chat feed is maximally sensitive to this. The detach/reattach + targeted-patch strategy is proven (xterm, Kombai iframe, #roomFeed) but fragile in a 4,900-line single file with ~40 mutable globals and an already-dirty working tree on feat/agent-room — coordination and possibly extracting chat into its own module (src/chat.ts) are needed to keep this reviewable.

Session-file contention: app-server threads and `codex resume` in a PTY write the same rollout lineage; running both simultaneously (or racing the escape hatch) can fork or corrupt history. The collapse_forks HEAD-file assumption in discussions.rs could silently truncate transcripts if a fork diverges from an earlier point.

Markdown introduces the first non-escapeHtml rendering path; DOMPurify must be bundled (CSP blocks CDNs) and every delta re-render must go through it — an XSS regression here executes inside a Tauri webview with IPC access.

Process management: one codex app-server child per open thread multiplies memory/auth refreshes and rate-limit pressure per account (shared with the pool feature); Windows child-kill semantics (grandchildren) and zombie processes on crash need explicit handling; JSON-RPC -32001 overload needs backoff UX.

Remote mode runs app-server processes on the cst-server host, where multiple browser clients may open the same thread; the single-parked-receiver replay pattern only supports one consumer, so multi-viewer chat needs either a fan-out or an explicit single-viewer rule.
effortEstimate: Roughly 5-7 weeks for one senior dev familiar with the repo: Phase 1 ~1 week (spawn/handshake/lifecycle is mostly derisked by settings.rs::read_server_rate_limits, the work is supervision + event plumbing); Phase 2 ~4-5 days; Phase 3 ~1.5 weeks (card renderers + approvals + sanitized markdown is the bulk of UI work); Phase 4 ~4-5 days (transcript parser reuses discussions.rs helpers); Phase 5 ~1 week (server.rs routes + WS replay + platform.ts + reconnect logic); Phase 6 ~2-3 days plus a stabilization buffer. Phases 1-2 yield a demoable vertical slice in ~2 weeks; the terminal UI keeps working throughout, so the rollout can ship behind a settings flag at any phase boundary.
